title: The Boy and the Filberts
text:
A boy found a jar full of filberts, the sweet hazelnuts he loved, and pushed his hand down through its narrow neck to take some.

He did not want just a few. He closed his fist around as many nuts as his hand could possibly hold and began to pull it out. But his fist, stuffed with nuts, was now much wider than the neck of the jar, and his hand would not come through.

He pulled and twisted and shook the jar. Nothing worked. He was not willing to let go of a single nut, and he could not get his hand out while he held them all. At last he burst into tears, stuck fast and furious at his bad luck.

A man who had been watching came over and gave him some simple advice. If the boy would be content with half as many nuts, he said, his hand would come out easily, and he could always reach in again for more.

The boy let go of half, slid his hand free, and had his nuts after all.
lesson: When you are stuck, check whether you are trying to grab too much at once. Taking a smaller piece now and coming back for the rest often works better.
